clinician.trajectory_summary: A 48-year-old man with controlled hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and metabolic syndrome presented with a 20-day history of subacute dizziness, nausea, and vomiting following lunch, initially misdiagnosed and treated unsuccessfully with acyclovir and dexamethasone at an outside hospital. Fever (max 39°C) developed 15 days after symptom onset. Upon admission to Nanjing Drum Tower Hospital, workup revealed peripheral leukocytosis (WBC 19.52 × 10^9/L) and blood cultures positive for Listeria monocytogenes (drawn two days after fever onset). CSF analysis demonstrated lymphocytic pleocytosis (394 leukocytes/µL, 72% lymphocytes) with negative Cryptococcus staining and no atypical cells. CSF next-generation sequencing confirmed Listeria monocytogenes (3412 sequences, 95.63% relative abundance). Cranial MRI revealed characteristic rhombencephalitis with lesions in the right pontine and brachium pontis. After diagnosis, high-dose ampicillin therapy (2 g every 4 hours intravenously) was initiated. Following a 50-day hospitalization, the patient demonstrated clinical recovery with return of normal consciousness and normalization of blood counts.
